mainTopic: Which sin the ציץ covers: why טומאה and not יוצא, the left hand, or a בעל מום, and how impure blood is accepted.
overview: The משנה rules that if the קומץ of a מנחה became טמא and was offered anyway, the ציץ makes the offering acceptable. If the קומץ went out of its area (יוצא), the ציץ does not help. A ברייתא reads the פסוק "ונשא אהרן את עון הקדשים" and rules out פיגול and נותר, so the sin the ציץ carries must be טומאה, which is allowed for the ציבור. רבי זירא asks why it is not יוצא, which is allowed on a במה. אביי answers that the פסוק says "לפני ה׳", so the sin has to be one allowed inside the מקדש. רבי אילעא suggests the left hand, which is used on יום הכפורים. אביי answers that there the left hand is the proper way, so no sin is pushed aside. רב אשי answers that the ציץ covers a flaw in the offering, not a mistake by the person. רב סימא suggests a בעל מום, since blemishes are allowed for birds, but רב אשי shows that the תורה says a בעל מום is never accepted. Finally, a ברייתא rules that impure blood sprinkled by mistake is accepted for an individual, while a communal offering is accepted either way. It starts on the rule for a גוי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ציץ helps for a טמא קומץ but not for one that went out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the ציץ makes a טמא קומץ acceptable after it was offered, but does not make acceptable a קומץ that left its proper area.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the handful became impure and the כהן offered it, the ציץ makes it acceptable. If it went out of its area and he offered it, the ציץ does not make it acceptable. That is because the ציץ works for impurity but not for something that went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a ruling about two problems with a קומץ after it was already offered on the מזבח: טומאה and יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ can fix the problem of טומאה after the fact, so the offering still counts. It cannot fix the problem of a קומץ that left its holy area. The משנה gives the rule but does not yet explain why the ציץ works for one problem and not the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
The golden frontplate worn on the forehead of the כהן גדול
Makes the offering acceptable, so it still counts
Became ritually impure
Something holy that left its required area (here, the courtyard)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya tries to find the source and reason for this difference between טומאה and יוצא.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If the handful became impure and he offered it,
the frontplate makes it acceptable.
If it went out and he offered it,
phrases.notes: "Went out" means the קומץ left the area where it has to stay.

phrases.english: the frontplate does not make it acceptable,
because the frontplate makes acceptable what is impure,
but does not make acceptable what went out.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ makes a טמא קומץ acceptable after it is offered. It does not make acceptable a קומץ that was יוצא.

steps.title: Which sin does the frontplate carry?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes the פסוק about the ציץ and asks which sin it covers, ruling out פיגול and נותר because other פסוקים already say those are not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: "And אהרן shall carry the sin of the holy things." Which sin does he carry? If you say the sin of פיגול, the תורה already said "it shall not be counted." If you say the sin of נותר, the תורה already said "it shall not be accepted."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that looks for the Torah source of the ציץ's power. It crosses out two possible answers, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ cannot cover פיגול, because the Torah clearly says a פיגול offering is "not counted." It cannot cover נותר either, because the Torah says it is "not accepted." If the ציץ fixed these, it would contradict those פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: "And Aharon shall carry the sin of the holy things" (the פסוק about the ציץ)
An offering ruined by an improper intention about eating or burning it after its time
Meat of an offering left over past its allowed time
"It shall not be counted"
"It shall not be accepted"

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying פיגול and נותר are fine. It is saying the ציץ cannot be the fix for them, because the Torah already said those offerings fail.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"And Aharon shall carry the sin of the holy things"
But which sin does he carry?
If you say the sin of פיגול,
it already says "it shall not be counted"!
If you say the sin of נותר,
it already says "it shall not be accepted"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the Torah source behind the משנה's rule that the ציץ covers טומאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific sin the פסוק means when it says the ציץ "carries the sin of the holy things."

steps.title: The frontplate carries the sin of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the ציץ covers טומאה, since טומאה is already allowed in some cases, namely for the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: So he carries only the sin of impurity, which was allowed out of its general rule in the case of the community.
steps.whatsHappening: After crossing out פיגול and נותר, the ברייתא answers that the ציץ covers טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why is טומאה a good fit? The Torah itself already allows טומאה in one setting: when the whole ציבור is טמא, communal offerings may be brought anyway. Since טומאה is not a total block, it makes sense that the ציץ can fix it in other cases too.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity
Was allowed out of its general rule, meaning there is a case where it is permitted
The community; here, communal offerings brought when the community is טמא

steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ covers טומאה because טומאה is already permitted in one case: the ציבור.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶלָּא עֲוֹן טוּמְאָה
phrases.english: So he carries only the sin of impurity,
which was allowed out of its general rule in the case of the community.
phrases.notes: When most of the community is טמא, communal offerings are brought even in טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֵינוֹ נוֹשֵׂא אֶלָּא עֲוֹן טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 once פיגול and נותר are crossed out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ציץ carries the sin of טומאה, because טומאה is allowed in the case of the ציבור.

steps.title: רבי זירא: why not say the sin of going out?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges the reasoning: יוצא is also allowed in some cases (on a private במה), so maybe the ציץ covers יוצא instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Say instead the sin of something that went out, which was allowed out of its general rule on a private altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks the reason the ברייתא gave for choosing טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא picked טומאה because it is permitted in one case. רבי זירא points out that יוצא also has a permitted case. On a במה (a private altar used in certain periods), there was no fixed holy area to "go out" of. So the same logic could point to יוצא, which goes against the משנה that says the ציץ does not cover יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: Objected to it, raising a challenge
Say instead
A private altar, allowed during certain periods when there was no fixed משכן

phrases.english: רבי זירא objected to it:
Say instead the sin of something that went out,
which was allowed out of its general rule on a private altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא אֵימָא עֲוֹן יוֹצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 3 for picking טומאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reasoning that the ציץ covers טומאה because it "was allowed out of its general rule."
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יוצא also was allowed out of its general rule (on a במה), so the same reasoning would make the ציץ cover יוצא. That goes against the משנה.

steps.title: אביי: the ציץ only covers a sin that is allowed 'before ה׳'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבי זירא. The פסוק says 'לפני ה׳', so the ציץ covers only a sin that is allowed inside the מקדש. That rules out יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The verse says 'that they may be accepted before ה׳.' A sin that is allowed before ה׳, yes. The sin of יוצא, no.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא's challenge. He explains why the ציץ covers טומאה and not יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both טומאה and יוצא are allowed in some cases. But טומאה is allowed for the ציבור right inside the מקדש, which is 'before ה׳‎'. יוצא is only allowed on a private במה, outside the מקדש, so the פסוק's words leave it out.

keyTerms.meaning: to be accepted favorably
before ה׳, meaning in the מקדש
sin or flaw in the offering
an offering that went out of its proper area

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the ruling of the משנה from Step 1: the ציץ helps with a טמא קומץ but not with a קומץ that went out of its area.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: The verse states:
"that they may be accepted before ה׳,"
a sin that is allowed before ה׳: yes,
phrases.notes: He means a sin that is sometimes allowed inside the מקדש itself, like טומאה for the ציבור.

phrases.english: the sin of an offering that went out: no.
phrases.notes: יוצא was only allowed on a private במה, which is not 'before ה׳' in the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a limit out of the פסוק's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since יוצא is also allowed in some cases, the ציץ might cover it instead of טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לפני ה׳' limits the ציץ to a sin that is allowed inside the מקדש, and that is טומאה.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: maybe the ציץ covers service done with the left hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא suggests the ציץ might cover the sin of doing the עבודה with the left hand, since the left hand is allowed inside the מקדש on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא objects: Say instead that the ציץ covers the sin of using the left hand, which was allowed out of its general rule on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא challenges אביי's answer with a new candidate. This one passes אביי's test, because it is allowed inside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the left hand normally makes the עבודה invalid. On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול carries the spoon of קטורת into the קודש הקדשים with his left hand, so this is allowed 'before ה׳' too. That fits אביי's rule just as well as טומאה does.

keyTerms.meaning: the left hand, which is normally invalid for עבודה
allowed out of its general rule in some case
the Day of Atonement

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a objects to this:
Say that the ציץ covers the sin of using the left hand,
which was allowed out of its general rule on Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: On יום הכפורים the כהן גדול carries the spoon of קטורת in his left hand into the קודש הקדשים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's rule by offering another sin that also meets it.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that the ציץ covers a sin allowed 'before ה׳'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the left hand is also allowed inside the מקדש on יום הכפורים, so the rule does not single out טומאה.

steps.title: אביי: on יום הכפורים the left hand is the proper way, not a sin pushed aside
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the word 'עון' as a real sin that was pushed aside. On יום הכפורים the left hand is simply the correct way, so it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The פסוק says 'עון.' That means a sin that was in it and I pushed aside. This leaves out יום הכפורים, because there the proper way is with the left hand.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי אילעא from the word 'עון' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With טומאה for the ציבור, the problem is really there, and the Torah pushes it aside. On יום הכפורים the left hand is not a problem at all, because it is the correct way to do that עבודה. So the left hand is never a sin that was allowed, and it does not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: and I pushed it aside, meaning the problem exists but is overridden
to exclude
its proper, valid way of being done

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the left hand on יום הכפורים is a sin that gets allowed. אביי's point is that it is simply the correct way there, so nothing was pushed aside.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him: The verse states "sin":
a sin that was in it, and I pushed it aside,
to exclude Yom Kippur,
where its proper way is with the left hand.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction based on the פסוק's word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The left hand is allowed on יום הכפורים, so it is a sin that is allowed in the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: On יום הכפורים the left hand is the correct way, not a real problem that was pushed aside, so it is excluded.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ציץ covers a flaw in the offering, not in the person
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different reason to exclude the left hand. The פסוק says 'עון הקדשים', so it means a flaw in the offering itself, not a mistake by the people bringing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The verse says 'the sin of the holy things,' and not 'the sin of those who sanctify them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second answer to רבי אילעא, separate from אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאה is a problem in the קדשים themselves. Using the left hand is a mistake made by the כהן doing the service. Since the פסוק speaks of the sin of the holy things, the ציץ does not cover the כהן's own error.

keyTerms.meaning: the sin of the holy things, a flaw in the offering itself
the sin of those who bring the offering, a mistake by the people

steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ covers טומאה because of three points. It is allowed 'before ה׳' in the מקדש, unlike יוצא. It is a real problem that was pushed aside, unlike the left hand on יום הכפורים (אביי). And it is a flaw in the offering itself, not a mistake of the person (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: "the sin of the holy things,"
and not "the sin of those who bring them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than אביי to the same challenge from רבי אילעא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The left hand might be covered by the ציץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ covers only a flaw in the offering, so a mistake by the כהן, like using the left hand, is not covered.

steps.title: Maybe the ציץ covers a blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: רב סימא asks רב אשי why the ציץ shouldn't cover a בעל מום. After all, blemishes are allowed in some cases: with birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סימא son of רב אידי said to רב אשי (some say it was רב סימא son of רב אשי): Why not say the ציץ covers the sin of a blemished animal? That prohibition is allowed in general for birds, since a teacher said: being unblemished and male is required for animals, but not for birds.
steps.whatsHappening: רב סימא offers another candidate for the sin the ציץ forgives: offering a בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule so far is that the ציץ covers a sin that is allowed in some cases. A blemish seems to fit, because birds do not need to be unblemished. It is also a flaw in the offering itself, so it seems to pass רב אשי's own test of עון הקדשים from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a physical blemish, normally unfit as a קרבן
The requirement that a קרבן be whole, without a blemish
The requirement that certain קרבנות be male
Birds brought as קרבנות

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סִימָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Sima son of Rav Idi said to Rav Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב סִימָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Sima son of Rav Ashi who said to Rav Ashi:
But say it covers the sin of a blemished animal,
whose general prohibition was allowed in the case of birds,
as the Master said: being unblemished and male applies to animals,
but being unblemished and male does not apply to birds!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא עֲוֹן בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁהוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ בְּעוֹפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new candidate that seems to fit רב אשי's own test of עון הקדשים
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ציץ covers only טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blemish is allowed for birds and is a flaw in the offering itself, so it meets every condition given so far.

steps.title: The פסוק says a blemished animal is never accepted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the תורה says a בעל מום 'shall not be accepted', so nothing, not even the ציץ, can make it work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About your point, the פסוק says 'It shall not be accepted' and 'for it shall not be acceptable for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the suggestion by quoting פסוקים that say a blemished animal is never accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ works by making an offering 'accepted' (לרצון). The תורה says outright that a בעל מום is not accepted, so the ציץ cannot override that. This leaves טומאה as the sin the ציץ covers.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be accepted
Accepted, bringing favor and atonement

phrases.english: He said to him: About your point, the verse says,
"It shall not be accepted",
"for it shall not be acceptable for you".

steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ covers טומאה, not יוצא, not the left hand, and not a בעל מום. The תורה says directly that a בעל מום is never accepted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An explicit פסוק excludes the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A בעל מום fits the pattern of a sin allowed elsewhere, so the ציץ might cover it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה states that a בעל מום is never accepted, so the ציץ cannot help it.

steps.title: Blood that became impure: by mistake it works, on purpose it does not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches: if blood became טמא and the כהן sprinkled it by mistake, the קרבן is accepted. If he did it on purpose, it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Blood that became impure and was sprinkled by mistake is accepted. If it was sprinkled on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a basic rule about impure blood sprinkled on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the ציץ at work on טומאה. If the כהן did not know the blood was impure, the קרבן still counts. If he knew and did it anyway, the ציץ does not save the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of a קרבן that became ritually impure
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Done by mistake, without knowing
Done on purpose, knowingly
The קרבן was accepted and brings atonement

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Blood that became impure
and he sprinkled it by mistake, it is accepted;
on purpose, it is not accepted.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not accepted' means the owner's קרבן does not count for him. It is not talking about the כהן's punishment.
steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: דָּם שֶׁנִּטְמָא וּזְרָקוֹ בְּשׁוֹגֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source about how the ציץ's acceptance of impure blood works in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure blood sprinkled by mistake is accepted. Sprinkled on purpose, it is not.

steps.title: Communal and גוי offerings follow different rules
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits its rule to an individual's קרבן. A communal קרבן is accepted either way, and it begins to give the rule for a גוי's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? For an individual. But for the community, whether by mistake or on purpose, it is accepted. And for a גוי, whether by mistake or on purpose, whether forced or willingly...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It says the mistake-versus-purpose difference applies only to an individual's offering. It then starts on a גוי's offering, and that sentence finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a קרבן ציבור, even sprinkling on purpose is accepted. This fits the idea that טומאה is allowed for the community. The case of a גוי adds a new pair, forced versus willing, but its ruling has not yet been given here.

keyTerms.meaning: When is this rule said? Introduces a limit on the rule
An individual's קרבן
A communal קרבן
A non-Jew who brings a קרבן
Forced, beyond one's control

phrases.english: When is this said? With an individual,
but with the community,
whether by mistake or on purpose, it is accepted;
and with a gentile, whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether forced or willingly —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's rule to individuals and starts listing other cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mistake-versus-purpose rule applies only to an individual. A communal offering is accepted either way. The rule for a גוי is still to come.
